description:
Operate on the quick-capture queue at buffer.md: capture entries, regroup and validate them, then flush them into logs/.

Subcommands:
  add TEXT — append an UNKNOWN entry (raw capture, no thread); blocks tend/flush until converted
  suggest TEXT [-y] — propose a structured add-* for raw text; INTERACTIVE unless -y
  add-text THREAD TEXT — append a TEXT entry
  add-ref THREAD TARGET [SUMMARY] — append a REF entry
  add-action THREAD TEXT [--due D] [--scheduled D] [--priority H|M|L] [--depends UUID8] — append an ACTION entry; also reachable as `tasks add`
  list [FILTER] — show the buffer with line numbers, optionally grep-filtered
  rm LINE_NUMBER — remove a single line by its number from `list`
  tend — regroup entries by (thread, date) and validate; idempotent
  flush — tend, then write entries to logs/ and clear the buffer

Flags:
  top level: --quiet suppress info output; place it before the subcommand.
  suggest: -y auto-accept the suggestion without prompting.
  add-action: --due YYYY-MM-DD applied on flush+ingest; --scheduled YYYY-MM-DD; --priority one of H, M, L; --depends 8-hex UUID prefix, repeatable.

THREAD is a resolvable thread like 'Projects/SGB'. add-action TEXT is '(Assignee) description' or just 'description'. add-ref TARGET is a wikilink target like notes/<stem> or Projects/X.

Examples:
  ["add-action", "Projects/SGB", "(Riaz Arbi) Send quarterly report", "--due", "2026-06-15", "--priority", "H"]
  ["add-text", "Processes/Admin", "Bank confirmed the new mandate"]
  ["list"]
  ["flush"]

Notes:
  `suggest` without -y prompts on stdin — never call it without -y; prefer the explicit add-* subcommands.
  `add` creates deliberately invalid UNKNOWN entries that make tend report a violation and block flush until they are removed with `rm` and re-added via an add-* subcommand. Use the structured add-* commands instead.
  Do not edit buffer.md directly; add and remove entries only through these subcommands and fix shape with `tend`.
  Ordering: capture with add-*, then `flush` to write logs/, then run `tasks` with no subcommand to turn ACTION lines into TASK anchors.
  `rm` line numbers come from `list` and shift after any add or tend — re-run `list` before each `rm`.
  Exit 1 on: empty text or description; empty description after an assignee; --depends not 8 hex chars; --due or --scheduled not YYYY-MM-DD.
